question.prompt: Una rolls \(6\) standard \(6\)-sided dice simultaneously and calculates the product of the \(6\) numbers obtained. What is the probability that the product is divisible by \(4?\)

solutions.title: Count the failures
solutions.explanation:
A product divisible by \(4\) needs at least two factors of \(2\), so count the rolls that supply fewer than two. An odd face supplies none, a \(2\) or \(6\) supplies one, and a \(4\) already supplies two.

There are exactly two ways for the product to fail:

1. All six dice are odd. Each die has three odd faces, so independence gives probability
\[
\left(\frac36\right)^6=\frac1{64}.
\]
2. Exactly one die shows \(2\) or \(6\), and the other five are odd. Choose the unique even die in six ways. For each choice, independence gives probability \(\frac26(\frac36)^5\), so this case has probability
\[
6\cdot\frac26\left(\frac36\right)^5=\frac1{16}.
\]

These cases are disjoint and exhaustive: any other outcome either contains a \(4\) or contains at least two even rolls, providing the required two factors of \(2\).

Therefore the desired probability is
\[
1-\frac1{64}-\frac1{16}=\boxed{\frac{59}{64}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
